evidence: verify-seed.sh really did run a fourth check (a per-file cmp of the seed's repo/ tree against HEAD) while both the script header and the README enumerated three; the merged header now lists seven criteria, so the enumeration was genuinely incomplete rather than a stylistic quibble.
guidance_note: when a docblock claims to enumerate a script's acceptance criteria, re-derive the list from the script's own pass/fail sites before pushing, not from the ticket's wording.

evidence: by_id was built from live rows only while relations was consumed unfiltered, so an edge into a soft-deleted row is an unguarded KeyError that the enclosing '|| fail' would then have reported as a content mismatch; the agent filtered relations to live endpoints at the boundary instead of adding the per-lookup check the reviewer suggested.
guidance_note: when one collection is filtered and another indexes into it, filter the index at the same point rather than guarding each lookup downstream.

evidence: bash discards a command substitution's exit status in argument position, so 'printf ... "$(horizon_sha256_file ...)" || exit 1' only ever tested printf; the agent reproduced it against a bundle with an unreadable file and got a digest built from a line with an empty hash.
guidance_note: capture into its own checked assignment every command substitution whose failure matters - 'cmd "$(sub)" || die' tests cmd, never sub.

evidence: 'find . -type f' matches only regular files while the function's comment claimed a digest over the bundle's entire content, so a symlink's target could change undetected; the agent took the reviewer's second option and refused non-regular files at the layout boundary.

evidence: the position keys were unpadded decimals sorted as strings at two sites, so '10' < '2' would have broken the file's own 'rank order IS queue order' claim at ten siblings; zero-padding makes the key sort correctly by construction at both sites.
guidance_note: when a generated key is later sorted as a string, make the key's own format carry the intended order rather than adding a comparator at each sort site.

evidence: a live child of a soft-deleted parent is neither a root nor reachable from any live parent's recursion, so position[] would miss it and the later comprehension would raise KeyError; the agent filtered relations at the boundary and also added the die() the reviewer asked for, which still catches the parent-cycle case the filter cannot.
guidance_note: when closing a lookup gap by filtering at the boundary, name the residual case the filter cannot reach and check it explicitly.

evidence: verify-seed.sh invoked diff, cmp and sed directly with no horizon_need for any of them, against a codebase whose sibling script carries a comment explaining why every reached tool is declared; the premise is a plain fact about the file.

guidance_note: validate a value into the shape its use requires at the point it is resolved - a name that becomes one path segment is a single-segment type, not a string.

evidence: same unfiltered-relations defect as F6 seen from the blocks-edge lookups; the single boundary filter closes the parent lookup and both position[] lookups on blocks edges together, which is what shipped.

evidence: wc, tr, basename and mktemp are all invoked directly by verify-seed.sh and none was declared, in the same block F7's fix had just extended for diff/cmp/sed with a comment stating the rationale that covers them identically.

the reviewer correctly separated this site from F2's fix (the seed's own local_id graph, not the lit export), but the KeyError it predicts is unreachable: the agent measured that lit import refuses a dangling parent, a dangling depends_on and a duplicate local_id before the python ever runs, and the merged verify-seed.sh now asserts those three diagnostics at lines 252-254; the agent nonetheless posted 'Plan: valid, fixing', implemented the guard, and reverted it in a later comment on the same thread.

evidence: the reviewer is right on the narrow point it actually presses: the shipped comment asserted 'lit rejects a dangling parent...' about a binary this repo does not build and nothing here asserted; the agent converted the assumption into three negative cases in verify-seed.sh and mutation-tested them, which is a better answer than the inland guard.

evidence: lib.sh does invoke 'LC_ALL=C sort' in horizon_seed_digest and cat in horizon_build_memento_snapshot, and neither was in the new list; the agent's round-1 claim that the tool map was total ('undeclared: NONE' for all four scripts) had been checked against a hardcoded pattern list that itself omitted sort and cat, so it confirmed a map against a map.

evidence: duplicate of F26 raised in the same round; sort and cat are genuinely invoked by lib.sh and were absent from the list introduced one round earlier to be complete.

a newline in a filename is legal on POSIX and would split one path across two lines of the newline-delimited find|sort|read listing, pairing wrong hashes with wrong paths silently; the merged lib.sh refuses such names at the same boundary that refuses symlinks, which is where F4's fix had established the bundle-content contract.
guidance_note: when a boundary is created to decide what an input may contain, enumerate the content hazards the downstream code cannot survive - links, embedded delimiters, reserved names - and refuse them all at once.

evidence: git ranks GIT_AUTHOR_NAME and its siblings above user.name from any config source including -c, which the agent reproduced directly; the -c-only pinning is unchanged from the original commit so the flag is not fix-induced, and the agent's note that verify-seed.sh could never have caught this - both runs inherit the same leaked identity - is correct and is why the fix ships with a hostile-environment re-seed.
guidance_note: when pinning a value a tool reads from several layers, pin it at the highest-precedence layer and name in the comment which layers were checked; a same-machine reproducibility check cannot see an ambient input both runs share.

evidence: --no-verify suppresses pre-commit and commit-msg only, and core.hooksPath was not among the -c overrides while init.templateDir was, so an operator's global post-commit hook could amend or append after the seed commit; the -c list and its comment are unchanged from the original commit, so the flag is not fix-induced.

evidence: the comment written by the F20/F26 fix promised 'no script checks for a tool it can never run' while the list still carried cp/find/sort, which pin-instrument.sh and verify-instrument.sh never reach - the remainder F20 named and the fix skipped; the agent's counter-argument is sound and verified in the merged lib.sh, whose comment now states the over-declaration as the accepted trade.

evidence: I reproduced all four cases on git 2.52: an empty core.hooksPath disables a configured hooks dir, disables .git/hooks as well, and never resolves to the worktree root, so the /dev/null half of the finding is wrong and the agent's measurement stands; the 'nothing proves a hook does not fire' half was right, and pointedly so - the agent's first attempt at the test shipped a post-commit file inside the seed, which git never looks at, and only the second version made the operator's global config hostile.
guidance_note: ship the assertion in the same commit as the neutralisation, and construct the negative test against the mechanism the fix actually intercepts - a test that cannot fail is worse than none.

evidence: the hostile git-identity re-seed was added by F32's fix and the README's Verify section, which narrates every other check, was not extended for it; the merged README now carries that paragraph.
guidance_note: when a change adds a check to a script whose doc enumerates its checks, extend the doc in the same commit - three of this PR's rounds contain a finding of exactly this shape.

evidence: the wrapped fail() string is in the hostile-identity check added by the same commit that reflowed F27's identical defect out of lib.sh; the agent's own reply concedes it is 'the same defect I reflowed out of lib.sh earlier in this PR, reintroduced in the code I added for it'.
guidance_note: after fixing an instance of a defect class, grep the whole change for that shape - including the code being written in the same commit - before pushing.

evidence: the header declares itself the list of acceptance criteria and enumerated four while the script had grown to six, the two new ones coming from the F32 and F19/F22/F28 fixes; the merged header enumerates seven.
guidance_note: a docblock that claims to be exhaustive is a checkable claim - re-count it against the code every time the code gains a check.

evidence: the agent reproduced the clobber directly ('cp -R seed/repo/. proj/' overwrote proj/.git/HEAD), so a seed assembled from a real checkout would silently supply the project's git dir and defeat the fresh-history guarantee; the merged lib.sh refuses a .git entry at any depth with -iname, at the boundary F4's fix created.

evidence: cat's only lib.sh use is a heredoc redirection in horizon_build_memento_snapshot with no pipe near it, so the pipefail-blame rationale the F26 fix grouped it under is false for it; the agent moved the declaration above the comment rather than writing a second copy of the locality reason lib.sh already states.

evidence: chmod (the hostile-hooks test) and cat (seeding_diagnostic) are both invoked directly by verify-seed.sh and neither is in HORIZON_BASE_TOOLS nor in the script's own list - new code written during review reintroducing the exact class this PR had already closed six times; the agent mutation-tested the added declarations by renaming them to nonexistent tools.
guidance_note: when a PR has already fixed a defect class, run its check against the code the fix commits add - the new code is where the class comes back.

evidence: the README sentence described the first, vacuous version of the hook test (a post-commit file shipped inside the seed) which was replaced in 0cd7454 by the hostile-global-config version, and the README was not updated with it; the script's own criterion 7 already described the real check, so the two docs disagreed.

evidence: duplicate of F41 in the same round on the same two tools; the agent noted the duplication and fixed both threads in one commit, which is the right handling.

confirmed vacuous: seed[-1] is link-sync.4 and conformance.depends_on is exactly ['link-sync.4'], so the duplicate-id mutation also created a dangling reference, and seed_is_refused asserted only that seeding failed - deleting lit's duplicate-id check entirely would have left the test green; the merged verify-seed.sh picks the donor from the reference graph and asserts lit's own diagnostic fragment per case.
guidance_note: a negative test must assert the diagnostic that names its own failure mode rather than a nonzero exit, and must select its fixture mutation from the data's reference graph rather than by index.

narrative: A 3680-line new subsystem reviewed five times, hitting the round cap; 44 findings, of which the agent accepted or re-shaped 41 and pushed back on one outright. The reviewer earned its keep on the two findings that would have shipped defects - the git identity environment outranking the -c pins (F32), and the seed repo/.git that would clobber the project's git dir (F39) - and on catching a vacuous negative test (F44). But 28 of the 44 findings exist because of an earlier fix in this same PR, and rounds 3 and 4 contain nothing else: every one of their eleven findings is a consequence of a round-1 or round-2 fix. Three engines produced them - a declaration list swept narrowly and then rebuilt wrongly in both directions (F7 through F34), a promised fix reverted in a later comment on the same thread (F18 producing three duplicate re-raises and then F44), and docs and comments left describing the code as it was before the fix (F29, F36, F38, F42). The agent's technical judgment was strong throughout - it reproduced findings before agreeing, declined two suggestions that would have introduced the very bugs they were aimed at, and mutation-tested most of its checks - which is precisely why the cost here was sweep discipline, not correctness.
guidance_observations: Every round-3 and round-4 finding was caused by an earlier fix in this PR, so two of the five review rounds were bought entirely by incomplete sweeps rather than by anything in the original change.

The agent verified its own totality claim ('undeclared: NONE' for all four scripts) against a hardcoded pattern list rather than against the files' actual invocations, and the reviewer caught the two tools that list omitted - a self-check that confirms a map against a map should count as unverified.

Posting 'Plan: valid, fixing' before testing reachability, then reverting in a later comment on the same thread, is the single most expensive move in this packet: it produced three duplicate findings in the next round and the chain that ended in F44.

Two of the agent's own added checks were vacuous when first written (the seed-embedded post-commit hook, the confounded duplicate-local-id mutation) and both were caught only by mutation testing or by the reviewer - a new check should be required to fail before it is claimed as evidence.

The reviewer opened three separate threads on identical lines (F19/F22/F28) and two on identical tools (F41/F43); address-pr-reviews answered each in full independently, which triples the reply cost with no gain over answering once and cross-referencing.

Doc-versus-code drift accounts for six findings across four rounds, always in the same shape: a check was added or replaced and the README or the script header that enumerates the checks was not extended in the same commit.

horizon/seeds/** is vendored third-party content held byte-identical by a provenance claim, so reviewing it can only generate unactionable findings; the exclude the agent filed a ticket for during this PR is still not present in .github/code-review.conf.
